text:
alex_support: customer reports unexpected 429s even after monthly credits refilled. they say UI showed +5000 credits at 00:00 UTC but API still returned 429 for ~12m. repro steps and curl included. 

marie_eng: which tenant and timezone? any repro payloads or streaming sessions open?

alex_support: tenant org-1892, timezone America/Los_Angeles. repro: run continuous curl loop hitting /v1/generate with prompt size ~800 tokens until you exhaust monthly then wait for 00:00 UTC. they attached this curl: ```for i in $(seq 1 10000); do curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -H \"Authorization: Bearer $KEY\" -d '{"model":"rwd-gpt-13b","prompt":"hi","max_tokens":8}'; done```

marie_eng: got it. two hypotheses: 1) token-bucket rate limiter state not force-refilled on monthly credit job (we refill balance but limiter counters still at 0 tokens), 2) UI balance updated but cache edge still serving old quota to gateways.

alex_support: they said deploy-bot announced refill: "deploy-bot: monthly-refill job completed for org-1892 at 00:00:05 UTC" but 429s kept happening until ~00:12 UTC.

@tariq_sre: I'll check rate-limiter and redis TTLs. can you drop a small sample of request ids from the 429 responses? headers include x-request-id and x-rl-token.

alex_support: pasted three ids in the ticket (x-request-id: r-01gA, r-01gB, r-01gC).

kevin_prod: quick note — our per-tenant burst allowance is separate from monthly credit bucket. if someone exhausts monthly credits the token-bucket still enforces per-second burst windows; refilling monthly balance doesn't always reset transient limiter state if refill path only increments credit counters and not limiter refill timestamp. we had a similar but shorter case last year.

marie_eng: good call. @tariq_sre, please verify if limiter tokens were negative or if the refill job also triggers limiter-reset signals. check redis key pattern rl:tenant:org-1892 and job logs for monthly-refill-run-2469123456.

@tariq_sre: quick findings: monthly-refill job ran at 00:00:05 and increased "credit_balance" in postgres. redis keys show limiter tokens remained at 0 and there was a high backlog of queued requests on the gateway between 00:01 and 00:11 UTC. looks like edge gateway keeps a local in-memory token shuffle and didn't fetch updated credit->limit mapping until its local TTL expired (10m).

marie_eng: aha — TTL mismatch between control-plane push and edge cache. control plane writes balance, gateway cache expires at 10m by default. monthly refill doesn't proactively push to all gateways.

kevin_prod: mitigation options: 1) short term: manually flush gateway cache for org-1892 (we can do a targeted invalidation), 2) medium: have monthly-refill job emit a push event to invalidate or update gateway cache, 3) long: change gateway to consult control-plane on CRITICAL transitions (balance from 0 -> >0) instead of waiting TTL.

alex_support: customer wants a root cause and a ETA on fix. can we do a manual flush now and notify them?

@tariq_sre: flushed gateway cache for org-1892 at 00:13:20 UTC and monitored: 429s stopped immediately. left a note in ticket with logs.

marie_eng: adding an action item: ENG to add a short push in monthly-refill workflow that sends a small "balance-changed" event to gateways (P0 for Dedicated and Hosted critical path). created ticket ENG-rl-589.

alex_support: replied to customer with explanation: UI shows immediate refill; gateways may still serve cached zero-limit for up to 10m; we flushed cache for them and pushed ENG ticket. customer accepted remediation and asked for timeline.

kevin_prod: estimate for push change: small publish/subscribe hook + idempotent handler on gateways, ~3 dev days + testing. I'll put it in next sprint.

marie_eng: thanks everyone. closing internal thread once ENG-rl-589 is triaged. :white_check_mark:
